transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. Have you had any questions about your surgery or recovery so far?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, thanks for reaching out. I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start doing some light gardening, such as brisk walking, gardening, light jogging, and gentle cycling, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's best to avoid strenuous exercise, lifting heavy objects, and activities like pilates or yoga, or swimming for a month. And don't forget to wear protective eyewear when doing activities like golf or tennis, which you can start about 1 week after surgery.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, that's good to know. Next, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use the preservative-free eye drops as prescribed. If you're running out, you can get some more from your GP. Just follow the instructions on the bottle, and don't stop using them unless your doctor says it's okay to do so.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the advice. I'm also experiencing a lot of sensitivity to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: Yes, it's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild, just wearing sunglasses when you're going outside might help. But if it's severe or you're experiencing significant pain, we may need to assess it further.
